**Tier G** — governance — identity, capability, delegation, audit · owned by `platform` · `public.projects`

**One row is** One modelling project: a named supply chain, owned by one modeller, belonging to one organization. It is the scope every other project-scoped table hangs off `project_id`, and it is the row almost every RLS policy in the schema reaches through to decide whether the caller may see anything at all.

`natural_key_intended` is `(organization_id, name)` and the declared constraint is `(modeler_id, plant_name, name)` — they are different claims, and the declared one is the weaker: two modellers in one organization may each hold a project called the same thing for the same plant. Changing it is not WP 2.1's to do; `natural-key` (§2.1 I4) lands in WP 3.3 and this row is one of its inputs. Recorded here so the gap has an owner rather than being noticed again in a quarter.

## Uniqueness

| Columns | Source | Constraint |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | column PRIMARY KEY | `projects_pkey` |
| `modeler_id` + `plant_name` + `name` | UNIQUE constraint | `uq_modeler_project` |

**Intended natural key:** `organization_id` + `name` — the key this
table's grain implies and the database does NOT enforce today. A statement about
what is missing, never a claim about what is there.

## Governance

| | |
|---|---|
| Read capability | any project member |
| Write capability | `data_editing` |
| Minimum project role | `editor` |
| Tier transitions audited | **no** — invariant `audit-actor` is not met here yet |
| Row-level security | enabled |
| Policies on the table | 4 — all carry a predicate |

Tier G rather than a data tier: `projects` holds no measured quantity. It is the SCOPE, and its access rules are the ones every other table inherits by joining to it — which is why WP 2.1 had to redefine 58 policies on 24 other tables to change one comparison. Read is org-wide (any member of the owning organization sees every project in it); write is restricted to the project's own modeller or a global `admin`. There is no project-level role between those two — a member cannot be given read on one project and not another, which is `subtractive-delegation` (§2.1 G3) having nowhere to attach. WP 2.2's `project_members` is where `min_project_role: editor` above stops being a forward declaration. `audited: false`: project creation and deletion write no audit row (WP 2.3).

### `organization_id`

The owning organization by uuid. This is what the public /v1 API authorizes on (`api_can_access_project`: `p.organization_id = p_org_id`), and it is the plane that survives a rename.

| | |
|---|---|
| Type | `uuid` |
| Grain | `identifier` |
| Unit | dimensionless |
| Added by | `20260709000002_super_admin_phase1.sql` |
| References | `organizations(id)` ON DELETE SET NULL |
| Read by the engine | **not traced** |
| Validated at ingest | — |
| Rendered at | *not yet recorded (WP 5.1)* |

> D27 lived here. `set_project_defaults()` stamped `NEW.organization` and never this column, so the one-time backfill in `20260709000002` was the only thing that had ever set it and every project created afterwards was NULL — visible through RLS, which compared text, and invisible to /v1, which compares this. WP 2.1 fixed the trigger first and then backfilled, because a backfill in front of a trigger that does not stamp rots at the next insert. Still NULLABLE: rows whose text org matches no organization row, or matches two, were deliberately left alone rather than resolved to a guess, and the dual read keeps them reachable. The count is a §15 question.
